title: What If a Whole Town Lived in One Building? In Alaska, One Does

scenes.text: What if your whole town lived in one building? In Whittier, Alaska, almost everyone does.
About two hundred people live there, nearly all in one fourteen-storey tower finished in 1957.
Inside: a post office, a clinic, a church, a police station, shops and a laundromat. A tunnel leads to the school.
Outside, a typical winter brings about 250 inches of snow. That's more than twenty feet.
The only road out is a single-lane tunnel, two and a half miles long, shared with trains. Direction switches every half hour.
And at about eleven at night, the tunnel closes. Miss it, and you're not driving anywhere until morning.

description:
What if a whole town lived in one building? In Whittier, Alaska, almost all of the roughly 200 residents live in Begich Towers, a 14-storey former Army building completed in 1957. It holds a post office, a clinic, a church, a police station, shops and a laundromat, and an underground tunnel leads to the school.
A typical winter brings about 250 inches of snow. The only road in is a single-lane, two-and-a-half-mile tunnel shared with trains, which switches direction every half hour and closes at about 11 pm.
